mekayis.metin:
(بَطَّ) الْبَاءُ وَالطَّاءُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ، وَهُوَ الْبَطُّ وَالشَّقُّ. يُقَالُ: بَطَّ الْجُرْحَ يَبُطُّهُ بَطًّا، أَيْ: شَقَّهُ. فَأَمَّا الْبَطِيطُ الَّذِي هُوَ الْعَجَبُ فَمِنْ هَذَا أَيْضًا; لِأَنَّهُ أَمْرٌ بُطَّ عَنْهُ فَأُظْهِرَ حَتَّى أَعْجَبَ. وَقَالَ الْكُمَيْتُ:
أَلَمَّا تَعْجَبِي وَتَرَيْ بَطِيطًا ... مِنَ اللَّائِينَ فِي الْحِجَجِ الْخَوَالِي
وَمَا سِوَى ذَلِكَ مِنَ الْبَاءِ وَالطَّاءِ فَفَارِسِيٌّ كُلُّهُ.

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: بَطَّ • (baṭṭa) I (non-past يَبُطُّ (yabuṭṭu), verbal noun بَطّ (baṭṭ))
بَاطِيَة • (bāṭiya) f (plural بَوَاطٍ (bawāṭin, construct state بَوَاطِي (bawāṭī)))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Borrowed from Aramaic, cognate with Classical Syriac ܒܳܛܺܝܬܴܐ (bāṭīṯā) and Jewish Babylonian Aramaic בָּטִיתָא (bāṭīṯā), with a possible mediary Old Persian *bātah (“wine, must”) from Akkadian 𒁀𒂅𒌑 (baṭû, “tray, platter; mixing container, bowl for liquids; wine jar, pitcher”), from earlier Akkadian 𒁀𒋾𒌝 (baṭium, “vessel, basin, place to hold; tray, platter”) shifting semantically by the Neo-Babylonian period, but consistently an item listed with sets of vessels. Ultimately derived from Proto-Semitic *bvṭ- (“a space or vessel; to be swollen, filled up, slow; to mix, agitate, or gurgle; to be hollow or emptied out, to lose or spread out contents”). Further cognates with Persian بادیه (bādiya /bâdiye, “deep earthen wine-jug”), Persian باده (bāda /bâde, “wine”), Ancient Greek βατιάκη (batiákē), Latin batiaca, batioca, batiola.
s: Akkadian 𒁀𒂅𒌑 (baṭû, “tray, platter; mixing container, bowl for liquids; wine jar, pitcher”)
Akkadian 𒁀𒋾𒌝 (baṭium, “vessel, basin, place to hold; tray, platter”)
Proto-Semitic *bvṭ- (“a space or vessel; to be swollen, filled up, slow; to mix, agitate, or gurgle; to be hollow or emptied out, to lose or spread out contents”)
